prose: but it can hand you json instead of a dict. so there's that. a call to a device that's never booted, the shim answers 'never booted' a call to a device that's down show's last known status and offline. every device has a chat window by default. that will take at least the same commands as the command line for that device. we could do as words or like skills or prompts or something with some prefix character. if the device has 'reasoning'... you do, librarian will, igor will... then it can chat-with-the-model who's getting a selection of tools they can use. other kinds of devices will have to be examined to see what they do. the embeddings generator should take any string given and give back the embedding as a string in that window. why the hell would anybody ever need that? Because then we can use it to prove to me it's working. bus commands can list devices or turn them on and off. in the uu we had a device who was the catch all for small scripting things that hadn't become their own devices yet. because it was all scripts, by design, it wouldn't be able to actually chat. but we gave it a chat window anyway. it's character was a dog called scraps from the diskworld books. so if you typed things other than slash commands at it, it would reply with a random number of 'bark! ' it was the only easter egg. but you see what i'm getting at. and all of this is shim code stuff except the actual query processing.
